claims.text: The nanoparticles initially have a solid, homogeneous, equimolar or near-equimolar FeNiCrCoCu distribution.
Cu surface segregation initiates the onset and governs the progression of melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu has a lower intrinsic melting point than the other constituent metals in the alloy.
Increasing temperature causes Cu to diffuse preferentially to the nanoparticle surface.
Preferential Cu diffusion produces a Cu-rich surface layer.
Cu enrichment lowers the effective melting temperature locally at the nanoparticle surface.
The Cu-rich surface layer acts as the nucleation site for the liquid phase.
Surface premelting triggered at the Cu-rich region propagates inward toward the nanoparticle core.
Nanoparticles with measurable surface Cu enrichment will begin premelting earlier than otherwise comparable nanoparticles without significant surface Cu segregation.
Progression from premelting to complete melting will correlate with the extent and continuity of the Cu-enriched region.
Nanoparticles with a uniform Cu distribution melt only when they reach the bulk melting point predicted for the homogeneous alloy.
An inert atmosphere avoids oxidation during heating.
The proposed mechanism applies when nanoparticle size permits significant atomic diffusion.
Nanoparticle supports or environmental interactions may produce alternative segregation dynamics.
In FeNiCrCoCu alloys, tensile-compression asymmetry increases with increasing temperature and Cu content.
Direct observation that Cu surface segregation triggers premelting in these FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles has not yet been conclusively demonstrated.
